text: The registry is the JSON Schema registry of the bank Kafka platform, with the Event Hubs Premium schema registry as the fallback; there is one subject per event type, named <topic>-<Event> (for example rwb.case.events.v1-CaseCreated), the compatibility level is BACKWARD, and the build and the producer and consumer libraries call the registry API.
why: The architecture fixes the schema format, the compatibility rule and the AsyncAPI contract per topic but not the registry product, the hosting or the subject naming, and the story must register the schemas and gate the build on Day 1.
read: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 21, 22, 42 and 43
impact: Subject names appear in the build configuration and in the producer and consumer libraries; a change is a registry migration with aliases, no business change.

text: Retry topics take the event topic name with the suffix .retry.1m, .retry.10m and .retry.1h, and the dead-letter topic takes .dlt (for example rwb.case.events.v1.retry.1m and rwb.case.events.v1.dlt); each service has one principal, its workload identity, that writes its own topic and rwb.decision-record.v1 and reads only the topics where the event catalogue lists it as a consumer; quotas are set per service at the platform default.
why: The architecture fixes the topic pattern, the partition and retention settings and the retry windows but not the names derived from them, the ACL principal model or the quota values, and the story must provision and test them on Day 1.
read: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 9, 11, 21, 22 and 35; Template and Rules v1 §R4
impact: Provisioning scripts, the ACL negative tests and the replay runbook assume these names; a change touches the topic catalogue and the ACL test only.

text: Resource names follow the platform naming library: a Blob account and container for documents with an immutable policy for legal types, a Key Vault per environment holding one AES-GCM codec key per Temporal namespace, and two MFT/SFTP endpoints (WIN outbound and debt-buyer outbound) whose PGP keys are held in the same Key Vault; rotation uses versioned keys on a documented runbook; the rotation period and the immutable retention periods stay open.
why: The architecture fixes the three resource types, the WORM requirement, the 15-minute single-file SAS link and the PGP transfer, but not the names, the rotation period or the endpoints, and the story must provision and test them on Day 1.

impact: Names appear in the deployment values and the runbooks; a change is a configuration change, no business change.
